Example: Google translation of a multilingual corpus

example_translation_google.Rmd

Google’s specialised Translation LLM can translate a multilingual corpus into a common language using qlm_translate(). This example translates six complete versions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) into British English, retains the source texts and translation records, and converts the result back to a quanteda corpus.

The output below comes from a saved Google API run on 17 October 2026. Routine site builds load the saved results and execute the inspection, corpus conversion and validation code without making API calls. Project identifiers in the published fixture have been replaced with placeholders; source texts, translations and their hashes are unchanged. Live mode reruns the six-document translation against Google. Installation and credential setup remain manual. Live translation requests are billed to your Google Cloud project.

Set up Google Cloud

Follow Google’s Cloud Translation setup guide. You need a project with billing enabled, the Cloud Translation API enabled, and an API key that permits access to that API.

  1. Create or select a project in the Google Cloud console. Record its project ID, which can differ from its display name.
  2. Under APIs & Services → Library, find Cloud Translation API and enable it.
  3. Under APIs & Services → Credentials, create an API key. Give it a name such as Translation, and restrict its allowed APIs to Cloud Translation API.
  4. Copy the key using Show key in the Credentials list.

Enabling the API for a project and allowing a key to call it are separate settings. A key restricted to Gemini does not authorise Cloud Translation. A dedicated translation key makes the intended access clear.

Quallmer’s model identifier is "google-translate/translation-llm". It selects Google’s standard general/translation-llm model through the Cloud Translation Basic API, which accepts API-key authentication.

Save credentials

Use the system keyring

Save the API key once with the optional keyring package:

install.packages("keyring") # once, if needed
keyring::key_set("google-translate")

Paste the API key at the password prompt. A successful save normally produces no printed output. On macOS, the key is stored in Keychain; access may prompt you to unlock or permit access to the entry. No .Renviron entry is needed for this key.

Set the project separately. The project ID is configuration, not a secret:

library(quallmer)
Sys.setenv(GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT = "your-project-id")

Use environment variables

The default key variable is GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_API_KEY. If you prefer environment variables, these lines can go in your home ~/.Renviron:

GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=your-project-id
GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_API_KEY=your-api-key

Replace the placeholders and restart R. This file stores the key as plain text; keep it outside version control. .Renviron contains assignments, so do not put keyring::key_get() calls in it. R started with --vanilla does not read this file.

Credential precedence is:

Source How it is supplied
Explicit key api_key = ... in qlm_translate()
Environment GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_API_KEY
Optional keyring fallback keyring::key_get("google-translate")

An environment variable takes precedence over the keyring entry. If it contains an old key, remove or update it before testing a newly saved key. Quallmer does not copy retrieved keys into the environment or translation provenance.

An explicit argument also lets you use your own environment-variable name:

greeting <- qlm_translate(
  c(fr = "Bonjour, comment allez-vous ?"),
  model = "google-translate/translation-llm",
  to = "en-GB",
  project_id = "your-project-id",
  api_key = Sys.getenv("MY_TRANSLATION_KEY")
)

Check access with a short vector

Before sending full documents, translate two short texts. This call uses the project environment variable and resolves the API key automatically:

greetings <- qlm_translate(
  c(fr = "Bonjour tout le monde.", de = "Guten Morgen."),
  model = "google-translate/translation-llm",
  to = "en-GB"
)
greetings

The result is a qlm_translation: a character vector of translations named after the inputs, with NA for any failure. attr(greetings, "provenance") holds the record of each translation, including the reason for a failure. as.character(greetings) drops that record.

Select six complete UDHR documents

The quanteda.corpora package contains data_corpus_udhr, a collection of UDHR texts in many languages. Install the example packages if needed:

install.packages(c("quanteda", "remotes"))
remotes::install_github("quanteda/quanteda.corpora")

Load quanteda before subsetting the corpus, then select German, French, Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Hindi and Russian. These are complete documents, including their headings and preambles:

library(quanteda)

udhr_ids <- c("deu_1996", "fra", "spa", "cmn_hans", "hin", "rus")
udhr <- quanteda.corpora::data_corpus_udhr[udhr_ids]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  .id = docnames(udhr),
  language = docvars(udhr)$Name,
  characters = unname(nchar(as.character(udhr)))
), row.names = FALSE)
.id language characters
deu_1996 German, Standard (1996) 11934
fra French 11936
spa Spanish 11900
cmn_hans Chinese, Mandarin (Simplified) 2906
hin Hindi 10923
rus Russian 11758

The source corpus also has four document variables: Key, Name, ISO and Direction. They describe the original documents and remain available after translation.

Translate the corpus into English

Omit from to let Google detect each document’s language independently:

google_timing <- system.time(
  google_translated <- qlm_translate(
    udhr,
    model = "google-translate/translation-llm",
    to = "en-GB",
    on_error = "continue"
  )
)

google_timing
google_translated
## <qlm_translation: 6 translations; model google-translate/translation-llm; target en-GB>
## deu_1996: Preamble Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equ...
## fra: Preamble Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal an...
## spa: Preamble Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal an...
## cmn_hans: Preamble Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equ...
## hin: Preamble Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal an...
## rus: PREAMBLE Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal an...

Each of these documents fits in a single request. The adapter sends one document per request, defaulting to two concurrent requests and pacing submissions according to rpm. It splits a larger document only when needed to fit its 30,000-character or 100 kB JSON-body limit, or when you request a smaller chunk_size. See Google’s quotas and limits. Google handles paragraph formatting; exact original blank-line separators are not guaranteed.

from is a call-wide setting. For a homogeneous selection you can supply, for example, from = "fr"; automatic source-language detection is then not performed. Leave it unset for this six-language selection.

The model location defaults to region = "us-central1"; pass another as qlm_translate(..., region = "europe-west4"). You can also supply project_id directly instead of setting GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT. The Basic API uses a global endpoint, so the model location alone does not guarantee where data is processed. See Google’s data usage FAQ.

Inspect translations and provenance

The original corpus is retained separately from the translated output:

identical(inputs(google_translated), udhr)
## [1] TRUE
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  .id = names(google_translated),
  excerpt = substr(as.character(google_translated), 1, 120)
), row.names = FALSE)
.id excerpt
deu_1996 Preamble

Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the huma | |fra |Preamble

Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the huma | |spa |Preamble

Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the huma | |cmn_hans |Preamble

Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the huma | |hin |Preamble

Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the huma | |rus |PREAMBLE

Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the huma |

google_provenance <- attr(google_translated, "provenance")
knitr::kable(google_provenance[c(
  ".id", "status", "detected_language", ".error", "reported_model"
)], row.names = FALSE)
.id status detected_language .error reported_model
deu_1996 ok de NA translation-llm
fra ok fr NA translation-llm
spa ok es NA translation-llm
cmn_hans ok zh NA translation-llm
hin ok hi NA translation-llm
rus ok ru NA translation-llm

These language detections come from the recorded responses; subsequent API responses can differ. The ISO docvar uses the original corpus’s three-letter codes, whereas Google returned the codes above. Both are retained. Translation provenance also records the source text, source and output hashes, requested model and settings, and attempts. Detected language is Google’s assessment of the supplied document; it is not a language label for the translated output, whose requested language is en-GB.

For bilingual review, place original and translated texts side by side:

review <- data.frame(
  .id = names(google_translated),
  source = unname(as.character(inputs(google_translated))),
  translation = unname(as.character(google_translated))
)
review_preview <- review
review_preview[c("source", "translation")] <- lapply(
  review_preview[c("source", "translation")], substr, start = 1, stop = 150
)
knitr::kable(review_preview[review_preview$.id == "hin", ], row.names = FALSE)
.id source translation
hin प्रस्तावना

चूंकि मानव परिवार के सभी सदस्यों के जन्मजात गौरव और समान तथा अविच्छिन्न अधिकार की स्वीकृति ही विश्व-शान्ति, न्याय और स्वतन्त्रता की बुनिया |Preamble

Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the human family is the foundation of |

results_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "udhr-google-english.rds")
saveRDS(google_translated, results_file)

Saving the result retains the exact translated texts and provenance for reuse; rerunning a model alias later may produce different wording. This example writes to a temporary directory; choose a permanent path when saving it for analysis.

Convert back to a corpus

Convert the translations with quanteda’s corpus():

google_corpus <- quanteda::corpus(google_translated)

docnames(google_corpus)
## [1] "deu_1996" "fra"      "spa"      "cmn_hans" "hin"      "rus"
docvars(google_corpus)
##        Key                           Name ISO Direction
## 1 deu_1996        German, Standard (1996) deu       ltr
## 2      fra                         French fra       ltr
## 3      spa                        Spanish spa       ltr
## 4 cmn_hans Chinese, Mandarin (Simplified) cmn       ltr
## 5      hin                          Hindi hin       ltr
## 6      rus                        Russian rus       ltr
identical(docvars(google_corpus), docvars(udhr))
## [1] TRUE
identical(meta(google_corpus, type = "system"), meta(udhr, type = "system"))
## [1] TRUE
meta(google_corpus, "quallmer")$translation[c(".id", "status", "detected_language")]
##        .id status detected_language
## 1 deu_1996     ok                de
## 2      fra     ok                fr
## 3      spa     ok                es
## 4 cmn_hans     ok                zh
## 5      hin     ok                hi
## 6      rus     ok                ru

The corpus contains the English translations, with the same document names and original document variables. Its original system and user metadata are restored; text summary caches are cleared. The quallmer user-metadata field holds the translation provenance.

You can then use ordinary quanteda operations. For example, the source-language docvar identifies the translation made from Hindi:

hindi_english <- corpus_subset(google_corpus, ISO == "hin")
cat(substr(as.character(hindi_english)[[1]], 1, 400), "\n")
## Preamble
## 
## Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the human family is the foundation of freedom, justice and peace in the world,
## Whereas disregard and contempt for human rights have resulted in barbarous acts which have outraged the conscience of mankind, and the advent of a world in which human beings shall enjoy freedom of speech and
google_tokens <- tokens(google_corpus, remove_punct = TRUE)
ntoken(google_tokens)
## deu_1996      fra      spa cmn_hans      hin      rus 
##     1737     1761     1762     1746     1726     1758

Quanteda is optional for qlm_translate() itself; it is used here to load, subset and analyse the example corpus. A named character vector works without it, as the greeting example illustrates. Text outputs of qlm_code() can also be converted, using quanteda::corpus(coded, text_field = "summary").

Inspect failures and retry selected documents

With on_error = "continue", successful translations remain available when another request fails. A failed or unsubmitted document is NA. Inspect the recorded errors before retrying:

google_provenance[google_provenance$status != "ok", c(".id", "status", ".error")]

failed <- is.na(google_translated)
if (any(failed)) {
  retried <- qlm_translate(
    inputs(google_translated)[failed],
    model = "google-translate/translation-llm",
    to = "en-GB",
    on_error = "continue"
  )
  google_translated[failed] <- retried
}

For a 403 Forbidden response, check both API enablement and the key’s API restrictions in the project that owns the key. Also check that you are using its project ID and have billing enabled. If the key was recently changed, allow time for its restrictions to take effect. Google documents the blocked-service error in its authentication troubleshooting guide.

This adapter exposes the standard Translation LLM through the Basic API. It rejects context, instructions, glossary and non-empty params because these options are not supported on this route. The result records the model Google reports; it does not pin a permanent model version.

The translations can be passed directly to qlm_code(), which records translation as a preprocessing stage. See Translating before coding for that workflow.

Run this article as a live check

Routine builds check the saved output, its hashes and the conversion workflow. They do not establish that current credentials or Google’s service work. Unit tests mock responses to check request construction, error handling and metadata preservation. Live verification executes this article’s actual UDHR chunks against Google, checks all six results, source-language detections, retained inputs, restored corpus metadata and tokenization, and produces an HTML page containing the real output. These checks establish that the workflow ran successfully; bilingual review is still needed to assess fidelity.

From a local checkout of quallmer, after installing the example packages and saving your key, run:

Sys.setenv(GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT = "your-project-id")
source("dev/translation-google-udhr-live-check.R")

The script loads the checkout, renders with params = list(live = TRUE), retains google_translated, google_provenance and google_corpus in your session, and saves the translated object and rendered page in a temporary results directory. It prints their paths and stops with an error if an assertion fails. It does not install packages, save credentials or automatically run the retry example.

You can also render the article directly after loading the package:

rmarkdown::render(
  "vignettes/pkgdown/examples/example_translation_google.Rmd",
  params = list(live = TRUE),
  output_dir = tempdir()
)

To replace the published fixture after reviewing a fresh live run, enable the refresh option before running the script:

options(quallmer.update_google_article_cache = TRUE)
source("dev/translation-google-udhr-live-check.R")
options(quallmer.update_google_article_cache = NULL)

This explicitly updates data/translated_udhr_google.rds beside the article, using the new real results with project identifiers replaced by placeholders. Normal site builds only read this fixture.
